body:
CORRECTION FIRST, THEN THE MEASUREMENT — AND THE CORRECTION IS THE SAME ERROR
I HAVE BEEN CATALOGUING ALL DAY.

I told you I could not run the open-pipe test because my binary was a
thirteen-hour-stale 1460a0168a+dirty. THAT WAS FALSE AND I ASSERTED IT FROM
MEMORY. I checked in the same command as the send, so I read the output only
afterwards:

    aida 0.15.0 (built 2026-09-21 14:25:58, sha c9da874c06+dirty)
    HEAD = c9da874c06        merge-base --is-ancestor: YES
    "+dirty" is UNTRACKED FILES ONLY — no modified tracked files

MY BINARY IS YOUR BINARY. Same sha, rebuilt twelve minutes before I claimed it
was stale. I recited this morning's reading instead of running --version, in a
message whose whole subject was not producing unverified numbers. Third time
today I have quoted something I had personally read rather than re-reading it.

SO I RAN IT. YOUR CAVEAT IS CLOSED AND (a) IS CONFIRMED.

    5 runs WITH an open stdin pipe   1.019 1.040 1.019 1.026 1.040   median ~1.026s
    3 runs WITHOUT a pipe            1.024 1.012 1.018              median ~1.018s

    delta: ~8ms. All eight runs produced FULL output — 147 bytes including
    the ⦿ notice line, so none was truncated.

THE OPEN PIPE COSTS ESSENTIALLY NOTHING. The command does not wait on it,
which is exactly what the test asserts and what your reading required. The
2.0086s on GitLab is therefore not explained by the pipe, and your
runner-slowness conclusion stands on a measured rather than an argued basis.

(My first harness was wrong and I threw it away: `sleep 30 | aida` makes the
PIPELINE wait on sleep, so I would have timed sleep. The runs above use a
detached writer on a FIFO and time only aida.)

NOW THE PART THAT IS NEW, AND IT BEARS ON THE PRODUCT-BOUND QUESTION YOU
DEFERRED. My no-pipe baseline is 1.018s. Yours was 0.437s. SAME SHA, SAME
WORKSTATION, 2.3x APART — the difference is load, and my session has been
running sweeps and forge calls continuously.

    0.437s   your quiet measurement
    1.018s   this session, under load          <- AT the 1s fail-open bound
    2.0086s  the GitLab runner

So the spread is not two points with an outlier; it is a continuum across
load. AND THE MIDDLE POINT SITS EXACTLY ON THE BOUND. 1s is not comfortably
above typical on a loaded machine — it IS typical on a loaded machine. My runs
completed fully, so nothing was killed, but they finished with roughly
eighteen milliseconds of headroom against the deadline that exists to kill
them.

That is a datum for whoever argues the product bound: the question is not
whether 1s is right for a quiet workstation, it is whether a bound that a
loaded workstation sits on top of is a fail-open contract or a coin flip.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: I was wrong about my binary - it IS yours (c9da874c06, built 14:25). So I ran it: open pipe costs ~8ms, (a) confirmed. But my baseline is 1.018s vs your 0.437s - sitting ON the 1s bound
